::: {#exm-paradigms}
#### Two views of a success probability

Suppose 55 of 91 independent trials succeed.
A frequentist treats the success probability $\pi$ as a fixed number,
estimates it by $\hat\pi = 55/91 \approx 0.60$,
and describes uncertainty by how much $\hat\pi$ would vary
over repeated sets of 91 trials,
for example with a confidence interval.
A Bayesian gives $\pi$ a probability distribution before seeing the trials,
such as the uniform distribution on $(0, 1)$,
and describes uncertainty by the distribution of $\pi$ given the 55 successes.
:::
